issues.legal_issue: Revenue officers may exercise revisional authority under a general land revenue law over an order made under a related special law when the two laws operate in pari materia and the officers act under them in a cognate capacity.
material_facts: A Collector validated transfers under a special law governing the abolition of proprietary rights.
A Commissioner revised the Collector’s order under the general land revenue law.
The two laws had cognate schemes, and the revenue officers exercised powers under both without a clear distinction between those capacities.
issues.conclusion: The revenue officers could exercise revisional powers under the general land revenue law over the Collector’s order made under the special law.
issues.legal_principle: The Court treated the Madhya Pradesh Abolition of Proprietary Rights (Estates, Mahals, Alienated Lands) Act, 1950, and the Madhya Pradesh Land Revenue Code, 1959, as statutes in pari materia. Because revenue officers exercised powers under both laws cognately, and there was no clear distinction between an officer acting under one law and the other, the revisional powers under section 50 of the Code could be exercised over an order under section 6 of the Abolition Act. The Court relied on no earlier cases.

rule.if: challenge_to_revision_jurisdiction and special_law_order_reviewed and cognate_revenue_schemes and shared_revenue_official_capacity

predicates.challenge_to_revision_jurisdiction: A proceeding challenges a revenue officer’s jurisdiction to revise an order made under a special law.
predicates.special_law_order_reviewed: A revenue officer made an order under a special law, and another revenue officer sought to review it under a general land revenue law.
predicates.cognate_revenue_schemes: The special law and the general land revenue law have schemes that operate in pari materia.
predicates.shared_revenue_official_capacity: Revenue officers exercise powers under both laws in a cognate capacity, without a clear distinction between those capacities.

issues.definition: When a proceeding challenges revision of a special-law order, and the two laws operate in pari materia through revenue officers acting in a shared capacity, cross-law revision authority exists.

issues.legal_issue: The availability of an appeal under a special law does not prevent a suo motu revision when the same authorities hold both appellate and revisional powers and no statutory bar prohibits revision without a prior appeal.
material_facts: The special law provided an appeal against orders made by revenue officers.
The Commissioner and the Board of Revenue had both appellate and revisional powers under the relevant laws.
The Commissioner initiated revision without a party first filing an appeal before the Commissioner.
No statutory bar preventing revision in those circumstances was identified.
issues.conclusion: A suo motu revision could proceed without a prior appeal because the same authorities possessed both appellate and revisional powers, and there was no statutory bar.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 84 of the Madhya Pradesh Abolition of Proprietary Rights (Estates, Mahals, Alienated Lands) Act, 1950, appeals were available against revenue officers’ orders; section 50 of the Madhya Pradesh Land Revenue Code, 1959, provided revisional authority. Both the Commissioner and the Board of Revenue had appellate and revisional powers. The Court held that, absent a statutory embargo, the absence of a prior appeal was an idle formality and did not prevent suo motu revision. The Court relied on no earlier cases.

rule.if: challenge_to_suo_motu_revision and appeal_available and authorities_share_appellate_and_revisional_powers and not statutory_bar_to_revision

predicates.challenge_to_suo_motu_revision: A proceeding challenges a revision initiated by an authority without a party first filing an appeal.
predicates.appeal_available: The governing law provides a right of appeal against the order at issue.
predicates.authorities_share_appellate_and_revision: The same authorities have both appellate and revisional powers over the relevant orders.
predicates.statutory_bar_to_revision: A statute expressly prohibits revision in the absence of a prior appeal.

issues.definition: When a proceeding challenges a suo motu revision, an appeal is available, the same authorities hold appellate and revisional powers, and no statutory bar applies, the revision is valid without a prior appeal.
